editorial:
If you're in the mood for a gritty backwoods horror flick, this third entry in the Wrong Turn series drops you right into the West Virginia wilderness with a group of unlucky travelers and escaped convicts. The story follows a prison transport bus that crashes in the middle of nowhere, forcing guards and inmates to work together while a family of disfigured cannibals hunts them down. The vibe is dark, bloody, and unapologetically brutal, with plenty of chase scenes through the woods and tense moments where you never quite know who will make it out alive. It's not high art, but it delivers the kind of raw, no-nonsense survival horror that fans of the genre often crave on a late night.

The acting is a mixed bag, with some performances feeling stiff while others bring genuine energy to the chaos. The pacing moves quickly once the action starts, though the story can feel a bit repetitive as characters run, hide, and get picked off one by one. The gore effects are solid for a direct-to-video release, and there are a few creative kills that stand out. If you enjoy mindless slasher fun and don't mind thin character development, this is worth a watch. You can stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your collection.
endingExplained: In the final act, the surviving prisoners and guards make a desperate push toward freedom, but the cannibal family keeps closing in. The last survivor manages to turn the tables and kill the main cannibal, seemingly escaping the nightmare. However, in a dark twist, the final scene reveals that another member of the cannibal family is still alive and watching, suggesting the horror isn't truly over. The movie ends on a grim note, reminding you that in these woods, nobody is ever really safe.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves backwoods slasher horror and survival thrillers.
